oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-01.question: In this challenge, Jesus teaches us to begin prayer with our urgent needs, before speaking of the Father.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-01.learningObjective: Review the opening of the Lord's Prayer.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-01.feedbackCorrect: The prayer begins with the Father and his name, not with urgencies.

feedbackWrong.true: Hallowed name and kingdom come before our petitions.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-01.hint: Remember the first line of the prayer taught.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-02.question: In Matthew 6:9, tap to whom Jesus tells us to direct the prayer.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-02.learningObjective: Review the addressee of Jesus' prayer.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-02.feedbackCorrect: All prayer life begins by calling God this way.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the first petition, after calling him.
feedbackWrong.b: That is where he is, not whom we speak to.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-02.hint: It is the word that opens the prayer.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-03.question: According to Luke 18:1, why did Jesus tell the parable of the judge and the widow?
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-03.learningObjective: Review the purpose of the widow parable.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-03.feedbackCorrect: The aim is stated before the story begins.

feedbackWrong.b: The widow speaks and insists: she is the example to follow.
feedbackWrong.c: The parable opens persistence; it does not close it.
feedbackWrong.d: The judge is a character in the lesson, not a practical warning.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-03.hint: The goal is in the first verse.

options.a: To teach to pray always and never lose heart
options.b: To show that widows should stay silent
options.c: To close the subject of prayer once and for all

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-04.question: Build Matthew 6:9 in the order of the text.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-04.learningObjective: Review the order of the Lord's Prayer opening.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-04.feedbackCorrect: Father, heaven, and hallowed name: the opening stays the same.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin with the call to our Father.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-04.hint: Follow the prayer word by word.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-05.question: In Matthew 6:10, we ask that God's rule called what would come?
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-05.learningObjective: Review the priority of the kingdom in prayer.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-05.feedbackCorrect: Before daily bread, his rule is asked for.

feedbackWrong.a: That is asked in the next verse, after it.
feedbackWrong.c: From evil we ask deliverance, at the end of the prayer.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-05.hint: It is what should come to the earth.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-06.question: What does Luke 18:3 communicate that connects to this context?
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-06.learningObjective: Review persistence within a life of prayer.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-06.feedbackCorrect: She is the persistence piece in this life of prayer.

feedbackWrong.b: She returned to the judge again, without quitting.
feedbackWrong.c: Her lesson is precisely to keep coming back.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-06.hint: See the widow's role among the three teachings.

options.b: Giving up at the first refusal

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-07.question: In Luke 18:3, tap who went to ask the city judge for justice.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-07.feedbackCorrect: Without a defender, she herself goes, returns, and insists.

feedbackWrong.b: That is the setting of the story, not the person.
feedbackWrong.c: He is the other side of the case she brings.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-07.hint: Find the woman from the same city.

oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-08.question: Build Romans 8:26 in the order of the text.
oracao-sem-or-04-desafio-08.feedbackCorrect: Help, our not knowing, and his intercession.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin with the help in our weaknesses.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-01.question: In Luke 18:7, the parable treats God as a just Father who defends his own, not as a reluctant judge.
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-01.learningObjective: Review the contrast between judge and God.
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-01.feedbackCorrect: The unjust judge is the contrast that makes God shine.

feedbackWrong.false: Jesus' question expects trust in God's justice.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-01.hint: Separate the contrast character from God.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-02.question: In Matthew 6:10, tap the little word that equates earth and heaven in God's will.
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-02.feedbackCorrect: Heaven is the measure of what is asked for the earth.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the rule asked for, not the comparing word.
feedbackWrong.b: That is the needy place, not the comparison.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-02.hint: Find the short word between the two places.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-03.question: How do the Lord's Prayer and the widow parable complete each other on this trail?
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-03.feedbackCorrect: Jesus' form and perseverance walk together in a life of prayer.

feedbackWrong.a: One gives the form; the other, constancy in it.
feedbackWrong.b: The teachings are for disciples in general, without restriction.
feedbackWrong.c: The whole trail joins them on one path.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-03.hint: Think of form and constancy together.

options.a: Both dismiss any form of prayer
options.b: One is for leaders, the other only for widows
options.c: Both treat subjects with no connection
options.d: One teaches how to pray, the other teaches to keep going

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-04.question: How do the opening petitions of the Lord's Prayer connect?
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-04.learningObjective: Review the order of the first half of the prayer.
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-04.feedbackCorrect: Name, kingdom, and will: the first half is all his.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin with the holiness of the Father's name.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-04.hint: Our needs have not even appeared yet.

options.a: The holiness of the name comes first
options.b: God's kingdom is asked for right after
options.c: His will is done on earth as in heaven

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-05.question: In Luke 18:1, to pray always is the opposite of losing heart called what?
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-05.learningObjective: Review the aim of the persistence parable.
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-05.feedbackCorrect: The widow's perseverance is the practice of that never.

feedbackWrong.b: Resting in God is good; the forbidden thing is another.
feedbackWrong.c: Silence can be prayer; the opposite here is a lost heart.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-05.hint: It is losing heart in the middle of the way.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-06.question: What links Matthew 6:9 to Romans 8:15?
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-06.learningObjective: Relate Lord's Prayer and adoption in the Spirit.
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-06.feedbackCorrect: The Spirit of adoption makes the cry Jesus taught.

feedbackWrong.b: It is our Father: prayer of children and of family.
feedbackWrong.c: Romans trades slavery and fear for adoption.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-06.hint: See the cry of those who were adopted.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-07.question: In Romans 8:26, tap what we confess we do not know how to do as we ought.
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-07.feedbackCorrect: A life of prayer includes admitting that lack of knowing.

feedbackWrong.b: That is how he intercedes, not our task.
feedbackWrong.c: That is the ground of the help, not the act confessed.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-08.question: How does the widow's story advance in Luke 18:4–5?
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-08.learningObjective: Review the turn in the widow parable.
oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-08.feedbackCorrect: Refusal, insistent return, and the judge's decision.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin with the judge's initial refusal.

oracao-cam-or-04-desafio-08.hint: His decision is the last part.

options.a: The judge refuses to answer at first
options.b: The widow keeps coming to him without stopping
options.c: He decides to judge her case at last

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-01.question: On this trail, to pray well is always to speak perfectly, never lose heart inside, and never need the Spirit.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-01.learningObjective: Interpret a life of prayer without perfectionism.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-01.feedbackCorrect: The trail assumes weakness and promises help, not perfection.

feedbackWrong.true: Not knowing how to pray is where the Spirit helps us.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-02.question: In Luke 18:7, tap for whom God promises to do justice when they cry to him.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-02.learningObjective: Review the promise of justice for the chosen.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-02.feedbackCorrect: Persistence rests on who God is for his own.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the constancy of the cry, not who receives it.
feedbackWrong.c: That is what God does, not for whom he does it.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-02.hint: Find the group after justice for.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-03.question: What reading sums up the life of prayer taught on this whole trail?
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-03.learningObjective: Choose the summary the trail supports.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-03.feedbackCorrect: Form of children, constancy of faith, and help in weakness.

feedbackWrong.a: The three texts speak of relationship, not technique.
feedbackWrong.b: It is our Father, in the plural, with a taught form.
feedbackWrong.d: The widow is praised precisely for not quitting.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-03.hint: Join the three teachings of the trail.

options.a: Master techniques until God is forced to answer
options.b: Each one prays alone, with no form or community at all
options.c: Pray as children, persist in faith, and depend on the Spirit
options.d: Giving up early proves true spiritual maturity

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-04.question: Which sequence reveals the theology of prayer on this trail?
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-04.learningObjective: See the three teachings as one path.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-04.feedbackCorrect: Children who cry out and are helped by the Spirit.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin with the Father whom the children call.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-04.hint: Intercession in weakness closes the path.

options.a: Children call God Father in prayer
options.b: They cry day and night asking for justice
options.c: The Spirit intercedes in their weakness

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-05.question: In Romans 8:26, the Spirit intercedes for us with what goes beyond words?
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-05.learningObjective: Review the manner of the Spirit's intercession.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-05.feedbackCorrect: When the word ends, the intercession continues in him.

feedbackWrong.b: Volume is not the measure of that deep intercession.
feedbackWrong.c: No composition of ours is required in this text.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-05.hint: It is inexpressible, greater than words.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-06.question: What links Luke 18:1 to Ephesians 6:18?
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-06.learningObjective: Link persistence and prayer in the Spirit.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-06.feedbackCorrect: Always, at all times, and in the Spirit: the same perseverance.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts say to keep going, not to stop.
feedbackWrong.c: Christian perseverance is precisely in the Spirit.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-06.hint: Compare the always of the two texts.

options.b: Pray in the Spirit at all times

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-07.question: In Matthew 6:13, tap from what we ask not to fall, at the end of the prayer.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-07.learningObjective: Review the petition for guard in the Lord's Prayer.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-07.feedbackCorrect: A life of prayer also asks for guard in the hour of testing.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the final declaration of trust, not the danger.
feedbackWrong.b: From evil we ask deliverance, one step later.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-07.hint: Find the test that can bring us down.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-08.question: Which sequence reveals the full logic of a life of prayer?
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-08.learningObjective: Understand the full logic of a life of prayer.
oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-08.feedbackCorrect: Kingdom first, constancy in waiting, and his will at the end.

feedbackWrong.default: Begin where Jesus begins: with the Father.

oracao-pro-or-04-desafio-08.hint: God's will is the final measure.

options.a: Begin with the Father and his kingdom
options.b: Persist without losing heart while waiting
options.c: Depend on him according to God's will

estudo:or-04-desafio.context: This challenge joins the three teachings of the trail: Jesus teaches to pray to the Father beginning with the kingdom, the parable says to persist without losing heart, and Paul shows the Spirit interceding in our weakness.
estudo:or-04-desafio.focusQuestion: Which of the three helps — form, persistence, or Spirit — do you need most today?
estudo:or-04-desafio.keywordGloss: Pray as children, keep going without losing heart, and count on the Spirit when words fail.
reflectionPrompts: Without losing heart in the wait
facts: Jesus' prayer begins with the Father and his name hallowed.
The bread asked for in the Lord's Prayer is each day's.
The parable was told so we would pray always and never lose heart.
God will do justice for his chosen ones, who cry day and night.
The Spirit helps us in our weaknesses when we pray.
He intercedes for the saints according to God's will.
